clue.text: Monk almost left devilish group of fellows

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
something devilish is wild and mischievous, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the word itself with its final letter deleted

explanation.surface: A monk has all but abandoned the brotherhood for a devilish band of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' applies to the word 'left' only, trimming it to three letters before the seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Menfolk are the men of a family or community, a collective group of males.

clue.text: Drug makes writing bolder one supposes

blocks.note: short for methamphetamine
going over pencil writing in ink makes it bolder

explanation.surface: Someone speculates that a drug might make their handwriting more confident.
explanation.walkthrough: METHINKS is an archaic single word meaning 'it seems to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methinks is an old-fashioned way of saying 'I think' or 'it seems to me', hence one supposes.

clue.text: Certainly not around since the first Christmas, Santa's first to give the present

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another
first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: an emphatic refusal
Anno Domini, the era counted from the birth of Christ
opening letter of Santa

explanation.surface: A cheerful Christmas sentence about Santa and his long history of giving presents.
explanation.walkthrough: AD sits inside NO WAY, and the S is added at the end; 'present' is the time, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the current time, the same as the present when used as a noun or adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Half of olives made into this?

definitions.text: Half of olives made into this?

indicators.note: half means only part is kept, so the second half of the word is discarded
to be made into something is to be converted, so the letters are rebuilt in a new form

blocks.note: the word with its last three letters deleted, keeping the first half

explanation.surface: A question about what half the olive harvest ends up as.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a large share of olives is pressed to make this product.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is pressed from olives, so much of the crop is literally made into it.

clue.text: Capital guy coming aboard boat party, say

indicators.note: whoever comes aboard ends up inside the vessel, so one piece goes within another
say asks us to go by the spoken form rather than the spelling

blocks.note: short for catamaran
a guy is a man
a do is a party
the combined pieces spoken aloud match the city's name

explanation.surface: A man joins a party on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nepali capital is commonly pronounced 'cat-man-doo', so its unusual spelling hides three ordinary words; a cat is a catamaran.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathmandu is the capital city of Nepal, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Lay sister originally holding not completely pious views

indicators.note: not completely means something is missing, so the word loses its last letter
to hold is to grip, so one piece clasps another inside it
originally points to the origin, the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: to lay someone, in slang, is to bed them
holy, cut short
the opening letter of sister

explanation.surface: A lay sister in a convent holding views that are not quite devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay sister' reads as a religious term, but 'Lay' is a verb here and 'sister' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholds means sees or looks at, matching views as a present-tense verb.

clue.text: Cold fish

blocks.note: first meaning: chilly and exposed
second meaning: a small silvery European river fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold fish' reads as an unfriendly person, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a raw, wintry landscape, and is also the name of a small freshwater species of carp family.

clue.text: End bit of house getting extension

blocks.note: a house is a home
an extension is a stretch

explanation.surface: The end part of a house is getting a building extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End bit of house' looks like one phrase about architecture; the definition stops at 'End bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straight section of a racecourse before the finishing line is the final part of any race or project.

clue.text: Pulse fast, nearly sick

indicators.note: nearly means just short of complete, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
ill, cut short

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat that leaves someone feeling almost ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but it means an edible seed; 'fast' is a noun, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes such as beans, peas and lentils, so this is one example.

clue.text: Meagre inflammation containing discharge

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid
to can is to sack, discharge from a job

explanation.surface: A medical note about a minor inflammation with a bit of discharge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests pus in this medical scene, but it means firing someone; CAN is slang for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means barely enough or insufficient in amount, a direct synonym of meagre.

clue.text: Wipe column that begins written correspondence, deleting endings

indicators.note: deleting endings instructs us to drop the final letter of each word

blocks.note: a tower is a column, less its last letter
a letter, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiping a column of text that opens a letter, trimming its line endings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That begins' tells us the first piece comes before the second; both lose their final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelette is a small moist paper cloth used for cleaning, the kind of disposable wipe sold in packets.

clue.text: Obsession - a state where one scrubs room regularly?

indicators.note: to scrub something is to cancel or wipe it out, so letters are removed
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a European country
alternate letters of the word, first and third

explanation.surface: An obsession with cleaning, in a place where people scrub rooms constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubs room' sounds like housework, but the alternate letters of 'room' are cut from the front of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is an excessive enthusiasm or compulsive preoccupation, which is what an obsession is.

clue.text: River in French South, flowing West

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means running right to left, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
sud is French for south

explanation.surface: A river in the south of France that flows westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places a river in France, but the answer is a great river of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river flowing through Tibet, India and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Bone formation of fractured scalp in particular

indicators.note: something fractured is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
anal in the sense of fussy or overly particular

explanation.surface: A medical description of how a fractured scalp forms in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs to the anagram fodder, not a container signal; 'anal' is the informal sense of fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal canal is the passage formed by the stacked vertebrae, a structure made of bones housing the spinal cord.

clue.text: Temporary brand repositioning

blocks.note: a make is a brand of product
a shift is a change of position

explanation.surface: A marketing note about a short-term rebranding exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand repositioning' reads as marketing jargon, but each word gives one half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift serves as a stopgap until a proper replacement exists, so it is provisional.

clue.text: Details of pitch from crucial name on contract

blocks.note: a key point is a crucial one
the name written to sign an agreement

explanation.surface: A sales pitch whose crucial details come from a signed contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sales presentation, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation, the sharps and flats at the start of a stave tell players which notes are raised or lowered, fixing the tonality.

clue.text: Burglars duck atop roof-edge

blocks.note: a teal is a small duck
the eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: Burglars crouch on top of a roof edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea leaves' is cockney rhyming slang for thieves; 'atop' places the duck above the eaves in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the phrase stands for thieves, and burglars are thieves who break into buildings.

clue.text: Kept in hole in criminal drug den

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a hole looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone held captive in a hole inside a criminal drug den.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the definition; the second puts O inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded teenager is punished by being kept at home, forbidden from going out.

clue.text: Wastes away, giving up fried food

blocks.note: first meaning: squanders bit by bit, as money or time
second meaning: pieces of food dipped in batter and deep-fried

explanation.surface: Someone losing weight after giving up fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wastes away' suggests wasting away physically, but it is the verb for squandering.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to squander in small amounts, and the noun is a battered, deep-fried piece of fruit or vegetable.

clue.text: One who makes universal truth into crap writing perhaps

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: the film certificate for universal viewing
a fact is a truth
manure is dung
writing is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A cynical view of someone who turns universal truths into rubbish writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so writing is one example of an R.
explanation.definitionFit: A manufacturer is a producer or maker of goods, so one who makes things.

clue.text: Log lying across motorway bend

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a caber is the tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games
M for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A log fallen across a motorway at a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' reads as timber on the road; it gives the Scottish caber.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight curve or arch of a road surface, a convex bend in its shape.

clue.text: Erotic pinch missing bottom: Good gracious!

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, and missing means it is gone

blocks.note: steal, without its last letter
an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by an erotic pinch on the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' and 'bottom' paint a saucy scene, but pinch means steal and bottom its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes sexually charged scenes, so it is a synonym of racy or sexy.

clue.text: A vegetable and a thick roe blended together

indicators.note: blending mixes things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: a vegetable and thick fish roe blended together.
explanation.walkthrough: The recipe framing hides that the three words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is an edible thistle flower bud eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Accumulate debt and float to an auditor? Good gracious!

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what matters is how the words sound

blocks.note: to run up a debt is to owe
a buoy is a float, pronounced this way in British English

explanation.surface: A nervous question about debts and floats to a financial auditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' pretends to be an accountant, but it means a listener; 'float' also suggests petty cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations expressing surprise or dismay, used interchangeably in speech.

clue.text: Pack of dogs carrying a plague

indicators.note: to carry is to bear something within, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a hunt is a pack of hounds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pack of dogs spreading disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plague' looks like a noun in this scene, but it is the verb meaning to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to trouble or torment them persistently, the verb sense of plague.

clue.text: Mind one tucks into fibrous food

indicators.note: tucking into something means slipping inside it

blocks.note: bran is the fibre-rich husk of cereal grain
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reminder to be careful as someone tucks into a high-fibre meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' suggests eating, but it means placing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of thought, and the word is used loosely for intellect or mind.

clue.text: Drink shouted for social reformer

indicators.note: shouting is speaking out, so we go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: a beverage is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink loudly for a reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: William Beveridge wrote the 1942 report that laid the foundations of Britain's welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: Beveridge was a British economist whose report inspired the National Health Service and welfare system.

clue.text: Looking upward: Good gracious, that's a big bird!

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking upward means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gazes up at a huge bird and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British cockney exclamation of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a gigantic legendary bird of Arabian myth, strong enough to carry off elephants.

clue.text: Allegiance swapping sides initially, shifting to monarch

indicators.note: swapping sides means trading left for right at the start of the word

blocks.note: loyalty is allegiance

explanation.surface: A subject's allegiance changes sides and shifts to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the abbreviations for left and right, so the opening L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalty is used for a royal person, such as a king or queen, collectively or individually.

clue.text: Moment before new seed splits

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters are formed into a different order

blocks.note: short for second
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moment just before a new seed splits open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splits' looks like a seed bursting, but it means breaking away politically.
explanation.definitionFit: A region that secedes formally withdraws from a federation, breaking away in the way a group splits.
